note: The client's claim about itself: which error codes it can mint without reading one from the edge's body (`mintedByClient`) and which it only ever recognises from a body (`recognisedFromServer`). The halves are declared here, not derived from the code — CloudContractCodeCheckTest checks membership against CloudRouteErrorCodes.KNOWN, so a code added or removed without this file fails the test, while which half a code sits in does not. The mechanisms on the socket path (what the client mints, and why): a missing or blank token yields unauthorized (CloudTurnRoute); a refused or failed upgrade, a dead stream, or a closed socket yields connection_lost and is a terminal turn failure with no fallback (WebSocketCloudTurnTransport); a text frame that does not decode yields invalid_response. invalid_request and internal_error are declared as client-mintable but nothing in the tree mints them today — no bare 4xx or thrown stream produces them since the client moved to the single socket transport — so treat those two as spec-defined rather than verified by code. specRevision is the revision of the spec table this claim was last checked against; bumping it is a deliberate act, not a side effect of an edit.
